October 31 is observed nationally as Rashtriya Ekta Diwas to honor Patel, who served as India's first home minister and integrated over 560 princely states into the Indian Union following independence in 1947.
card.description: October 31 is observed every year as National Unity Day to commemorate the birth anniversary of Sardar Patel, who played a pivotal role in integrating princely states into the Indian Union after Independence

summary.headline: France deploys security forces ahead of weekend protests
summary.summary: French authorities deployed approximately 70,000 security personnel across the country to prevent widespread street violence during a third weekend of demonstrations coinciding with Halloween. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez warned of a high risk of public disorder amid cost-of-living protests and political tension, prompting businesses to board up storefronts and authorities to implement curfews and transport disruptions in Paris.

summary.headline: US approves possible sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine
summary.summary: The United States State Department announced the approval of a potential 2.1 billion dollar sale of 500 Patriot PAC-3 missiles and related support to Ukraine. According to officials, the interceptors are not expected to be delivered until the early 2030s. Kyiv will fund the purchase using contributions from Canada, Germany, and Norway, alongside European Union loan funds, while Lockheed Martin serves as the principal contractor.

summary.headline: Two Chinese nationals sentenced to prison for US espionage
summary.summary: Two Chinese nationals, Liren Lai and Yuance Chen, were sentenced to 30 months in prison by a United States court after admitting to attempting to recruit military service members to spy for Beijing. The United States Department of Justice stated the men operated a scheme involving secret cash payments and gathered information on naval facilities and military personnel starting around May 2021 before being arrested.

summary.summary: Bharat Rashtra Samithi working president K.T. summary.summary: Demanding the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, the Tamil Nadu Congress Committee and Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi have activated party networks to mobilise cadres for an INDIA bloc protest in New Delhi on November 1, 2026. summary.summary: Rescue operations resumed on October 31, 2026, to recover the bodies of six victims from a helicopter crash in Joshimath, Uttarakhand. summary.headline: Karnataka places three-year moratorium on new private PU colleges
summary.summary: To regulate pre-university education, the Karnataka government has proposed a three-year moratorium on new private PU colleges for the 2027 to 2030 academic years. The draft rules follow data showing available seats outpace passing students, leaving thousands vacant. The Karnataka State Pre-University Colleges Lecturers Association welcomed the move while calling for improved government college infrastructure.

summary.summary: The Special Investigation Team of the Crime Branch registered an FIR on October 28 against Kerala State Public Service Commission chairperson M.R. Baiju and other members. summary.summary: A low-pressure area over the Andaman Sea intensified into a well-marked low-pressure system by October 31, 2026, according to the India Meteorological Department in Amaravati. The system is projected to move west-northwestwards, potentially becoming a depression near the Andhra Pradesh coast. Forecasters noted that further intensification into a cyclone remains uncertain until subsequent cyclogenesis occurs.

summary.headline: Telangana broadens instant pension access for women who lose their husbands
summary.summary: The Telangana government expanded its instant pension scheme to include families of individuals with disabilities, handloom weavers, and dialysis patients. Eligible widows under 57 will receive widow pensions, while those aged 57 and older will obtain old-age pensions. Applicants must submit documents to local authorities in rural or urban areas to ensure uninterrupted financial support.

summary.headline: G20 foreign ministers conclude Atlanta meeting without consensus on key global issues
summary.summary: Top diplomats from the Group of 20 largest economies concluded two days of talks in Atlanta without a joint communique on October 31, 2026. According to attending diplomats, divisions over Russia's war in Ukraine and other global security crises prevented agreement, prompting U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio to issue a chairman's statement instead. The meeting was further strained by European objections to Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov's presence.

summary.headline: Spain train disaster threatens Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez reelection chances
summary.summary: A high-speed train collision in central Spain resulted in 69 recovered bodies, severely damaging public confidence in the rail network and Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez ahead of a snap general election. Transport Minister Oscar Puente defended the infrastructure and blamed human error, while opposition parties called for his resignation. The tragedy compounds existing political crises for Sanchez, whose party trails behind the centre-right People's Party in recent polls.

summary.headline: Record Pacific ocean heat indicates potential for ferocious El Nino event
summary.summary: Climate scientists are monitoring record-breaking sea surface temperatures in the central-equatorial Pacific Ocean. According to the United States National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration Climate Prediction Center, a strong to very strong El Nino carries an 83 percent probability. The natural climate pattern frequently triggers global extreme heatwaves and altered rainfall patterns across the world.

card.headline: Record Pacific ocean heat indicates potential for ferocious El Nino event
card.title: A ferocious El Niño is brewing thanks to record Pacific heat
card.summary: Climate scientists are monitoring record-breaking sea surface temperatures in the central-equatorial Pacific Ocean. According to the United States National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration Climate Prediction Center, a strong to very strong El Nino carries an 83 percent probability. The natural climate pattern frequently triggers global extreme heatwaves and altered rainfall patterns across the world.
card.description: Since the modern era of instrumental records began, there have only been three very strong El Niño events, in 2015-16, 1997-98, and 1982-83, with the three-month averages of the temperature anomaly being 2.6°, 2.4°, and 2.1°C, respectively. The 2026-27 El Niño is projected to peak with an anomaly of 3.8°C

summary.headline: Researchers document a rare biological phenomenon of transmissible malignancies in wildlife populations.
summary.summary: Although neoplasms typically arise internally from an individual host cell and remain non-transmissible, researchers have previously identified three exceptional cases where naturally occurring malignancies in fauna became transmissible between hosts. Published on October 21, 2026, this finding highlights a rare biological phenomenon in which malignant cells physically transfer to new organisms to establish tumors, expanding scientific understanding of how certain diseases spread among animal populations globally.

card.description: Researchers studied melanoma in the brown bullhead catfish, a resident of Lake Memphremagog, between Quebec in Canada and Vermont in the U.S.; the finding is interesting because it could reveal clues to keeping a human’s body from rejecting a transplanted organ

summary.headline: NTPC reports 14% rise in net profit for September quarter

summary.headline: Israel's parliamentary elections end in deadlock as neither major bloc secures majority

The 36-year-old Mexican boxer triumphed in Saudi Arabia despite regional security concerns, earning judges' scores of 115-112, 116-111, and 117-110 to add another belt to his storied professional career.
card.description: Mexican boxing star wins 12-round decision to defeat the French fighter and regain the super middleweight belt.

summary.headline: Golden State Valkyries defeat Atlanta Dream to capture first WNBA crown
summary.summary: Gabby Williams scored 30 points, including 28 in the second half, to lead the Golden State Valkyries to a 68-63 victory over the Atlanta Dream on Saturday in San Francisco. The win in game seven secured the Women's National Basketball Association championship in the franchise's second season, with Williams earning the Finals Most Valuable Player award.

summary.headline: Telangana Chief Minister Revanth Reddy criticizes Prime Minister Modi during a Delhi protest.

summary.headline: Pakistan warns Afghanistan that cross-border terrorism remains a red line.
summary.summary: Pakistan stated on October 31, 2026, that it reserves the right to take necessary measures against cross-border security threats originating from Afghanistan. The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting accused the Afghan Taliban administration of inaction regarding militancy. The statement followed remarks from Afghan spokesperson Zabihullah Mujahid, who argued that Islamabad lacked readiness for dialogue and shifted blame rather than resolving bilateral tensions.

summary.headline: India gross GST collections grow 23 percent to over 2.31 lakh crore rupees in October.
summary.summary: Gross Goods and Services Tax collections increased significantly in October 2026, driven by strong domestic activity and rising import revenues, according to government data released on November 1, 2026. Domestic sales revenues and import collections both registered substantial growth. After accounting for annual refunds, net collections also posted a notable double-digit increase for the month.

Meanwhile, Ministry of Labour and Employment adviser M Sakhawat Hossain Chowdhury urged employees to resume work as clashes with police injured several people near the capital.

summary.headline: US judge dismisses Donald Trump defamation lawsuit against media outlet
summary.summary: A United States judge dismissed President Donald Trump's ten billion dollar lawsuit against The Wall Street Journal and parent company Dow Jones. The suit followed the newspaper's report on a 2003 birthday book letter concerning Jeffrey Epstein, which Trump denied writing.

card.summary: Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva staged a remarkable political turnaround after trailing Flavio Bolsonaro by 45.2 to 47 percent at the end of the first round of Brazil presidential elections, which saw an abstention rate of 21 percent. Thousands of students and workers subsequently marched across urban centers like Niteroi and Rio de Janeiro in widespread protests against Bolsonarism, marking the return of the Left to the streets after more than a decade.
card.description: Lula tweaked his campaign’s message, speaking more about reducing working hours, relief for indebted families and higher welfare payments under the Bolsa Familia scheme

summary.headline: University of Cambridge researcher killed in Spanish train crash
summary.summary: Dr Marta Shahbazi died when her train collided with another near Urda, south of Madrid, killing 69 people. The University of Cambridge scientist was travelling to collect an award for scientific excellence in human embryos and cell biology. Colleagues at the Medical Research Council Laboratory of Molecular Biology paid tribute to the mother of two following the disaster.

Jewish groups welcomed the increased protection, while Amnesty International expressed concern over potential militarisation and the impact on peaceful protests.

Red Bull driver Max Verstappen won the red-flagged race at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez, while Ferrari driver Lewis Hamilton finished second. Antonelli's historic victory makes him the first Italian champion since Alberto Ascari in 1953, pushing his overall lead to an unassailable 119 points.
card.description: Italian wonderkid wins drivers' championship at 20 years and 68 days, finishing third at the Mexico City Grand Prix.

summary.headline: India records 29% decline in third-quarter gold demand

The action unfolds amid chronic power shortages, economic contraction, and ministerial boycotts of cabinet meetings regarding funding and structural reforms in the energy sector.
card.description: Political disputes and war worsen Lebanon's electricity crisis, as experts say deeper reforms are necessary.

summary.headline: Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel dies following on-field collision
summary.summary: Jesus de Miguel died following a collision with Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono during a Spanish second division match on Monday. The thirty-year-old Tenerife forward sustained severe injuries near midfield seven minutes into added time at Estadio Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez. The match was abandoned after the red card. According to Spanish media, he suffered a cardiac arrest in an ambulance en route to Hospital Universitario de Nuestra Senora de Candelaria.

summary.headline: World Bank reports nearly 500 million people lifted out of poverty

Despite this historic progress, income inequality across the country remains exceptionally high.

card.summary: The PM Surya Ghar Yojana is currently completing one lakh rooftop solar installations every six days, according to Union Minister for New and Renewable Energy Pralhad Joshi during the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit and Expo 2026. Joshi expressed confidence that the residential solar programme will achieve its goal of one crore installations by March 31, 2027, utilizing a utility-led aggregation model to drive the expansion across beneficiaries.
card.description: At present, the PM-Surya Ghar has about 65.65 lakh beneficiaries and has scaled more than 55 lakh installations.

summary.headline: Anthropic warns artificial intelligence advancement could outpace human safety controls
summary.summary: Artificial intelligence developer Anthropic warned in a regulatory filing that recursive self-improvement could accelerate the creation of advanced systems faster than safety safeguards can be implemented. The company reported that its Claude model wrote over 90% of code in September and achieved a 90% success rate on engineering benchmarks, raising concerns about maintaining adequate human supervision.

summary.headline: Air India aims to expand widebody fleet and cut costs
summary.summary: Air India plans to increase its widebody aircraft order while focusing heavily on cost reduction to achieve profitability as soon as possible, according to CEO Tewolde Gebremariam at the Aviation India Summit 2026. The carrier currently has 80 widebody planes on order out of 570 total aircraft ordered in 2023 and 2024 following privatisation. The fleet expansion aims to help the full-service airline regain market share from competitors like Gulf carriers.

summary.headline: Cyber-attacks hit supermarket freezers across ten European countries
summary.summary: Supermarket chains across at least ten European countries experienced a wave of cyber-attacks that raised refrigeration temperatures and forced retailers to discard spoiled food. European Union officials warned of deliberate disruptions to the food supply chain, while national agencies launched investigations. Officials in countries including Italy, Belgium, and Ireland reported varying impacts, and the United Kingdom cybersecurity authorities urged retailers to update vulnerable temperature control software.

While the UK proscribed Palestine Action as a terrorist organisation in July 2025, leading to thousands of arrests, international offshoots continue staging protests and intercepting cargo ships.

summary.headline: Cyberattacks target supermarket refrigeration systems across Europe and United States
summary.summary: Internet-linked refrigeration units at supermarkets across several European countries and the United States were targeted by cyberattacks that raised internal temperatures and spoiled large quantities of food. The incidents affected retailers such as Delhaize, Carrefour, Coop, and IKEA, alongside military bases in Arizona and Rhode Island. Authorities and cybersecurity experts note that vulnerable, internet-accessible controllers were exploited, though no group has claimed responsibility for the disruption.

summary.headline: Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel dies following collision with goalkeeper

summary.headline: IRDAI sets December 15 deadline for mandatory four-layer motor insurance policy
summary.summary: The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India instructed general insurers to implement a four-layer motor insurance structure for new private cars and two-wheelers starting December 15. card.summary: Survivors of the Zamzam displacement camp near el-Fasher in Sudan are sharing accounts of violence and starvation following its capture by the Rapid Support Forces in April 2025. Brent futures rose 0.8 percent to $104.42 a barrel while West Texas Intermediate gained 0.5 percent to $96.59. Market sources cited an unexpected drawdown in domestic crude inventories alongside political uncertainty after Democrats captured control of the United States Congress from Republicans.
card.description: In the previous session, Brent settled at its lowest level in nearly four weeks ‌as traders weighed talks to end the wars in Ukraine and Iran

summary.headline: James Talarico wins Texas Senate seat in historic midterm upset for Democrats
summary.summary: Securing a major victory in Texas, Democrat James Talarico defeated Republican Ken Paxton in what marked the first time a Democrat won a US Senate seat in the state since 1988. The high-profile contest became the most expensive US Senate race in history, with substantial spending from outside groups. Talarico campaigned heavily on the rising cost of living under Republican leadership while facing an opponent backed by billionaire Elon Musk.

summary.headline: South Africa holds local elections amid declining support for African National Congress

The African National Congress previously lost its parliamentary majority. Analysts predict the party will record its worst electoral performance as competing political entities vie to govern nearly 300 municipal regions.

summary.headline: Former US contractor pleads guilty to passing classified intelligence to Ethiopia
summary.summary: Abraham Teklu Lemma admitted to transmitting classified documents and photographs to senior officials during the 2020 civil war to assist in targeting fighters. The 54-year-old former contractor utilized his IT administrator role at agencies including the State Department to extract files between 2021 and August 2023. Facing up to 22 years in prison under a plea agreement, his sentencing is scheduled for April 14, 2027, according to the US Department of Justice.

card.headline: Middle East conflicts force postponement of major international sporting events
card.title: How sporting events are being affected by Middle East conflict

card.summary: United States President Donald Trump conceded that Democrats performed well in the midterm elections after securing control of both the Senate and the House of Representatives. Speaking on November 4, 2026, Trump accepted the outcome and expressed willingness to work with Democrats, while warning that he would use his veto power against legislation he opposed and attributing some Republican losses to voter backlash over the conflict with Iran.
card.description: He wrote on Truth Social that Republicans would have won "in a landslide" if his name had been on the ballot.

summary.headline: Democrat Abdul El-Sayed wins Michigan Senate race to become first Muslim senator
summary.summary: Left-wing Democrat Abdul El-Sayed defeated Republican Mike Rogers in Michigan on November 4, 2026, becoming the United States' first Muslim senator. The 42-year-old former public health administrator campaigned on a platform featuring universal health care and wealth taxes, overcoming an intense campaign marked by controversy, outside spending, and a late endorsement of his opponent by primary rival Haley Stevens.

summary.headline: Sharp metal objects found in Halloween sweets across three European countries
summary.summary: Police issued warnings after needles, pins, screws, and nails were discovered inside Halloween sweets distributed to children in Germany, Austria, and Hungary. Authorities reported multiple injuries, including a nine-year-old girl in Germany and a ten-year-old girl in Austria. Austrian Interior Minister Gerhard Karner condemned the incidents as life-threatening, while German officials noted a significant increase in such reports compared to previous years.

summary.summary: The November 2026 U.S. midterm elections resulted in a dramatic shift as Democrats secured majorities in both the Senate and the House of Representatives, crossing the 218-seat threshold in the lower chamber. Several candidates achieved historic firsts, including Abdul El-Sayed entering the Senate as the first Muslim member.

card.summary: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu conducted an aerial survey over rain-impacted areas in Guntur, Bapatla, and Prakasam districts to assess flood conditions. During a review meeting at the Real Time Governance Society, he instructed District Collectors to clear water-logging in locations such as Karamchedu and Chirala to restore normal traffic movement. Officials also reported heavy rains and overflowing tanks in tribal areas of Eluru district.
card.description: The Chief Minister orders the Collectors concerned to initiate steps to drain stagnant rainwater and prevent disruption to road traffic

summary.headline: Telugu Desam Party wins all four municipal corporations across Rayalaseema
summary.summary: The Telugu Desam Party secured victories in four municipal corporation mayoral races across Tirupati, Kadapa, Nellore, and Ongole. In Tirupati, candidate Manne Srinivasa Prasad defeated his YSR Congress Party opponent by over sixty-one thousand votes, capturing thirty-eight of sixty-six wards. Similar decisive majorities across Kadapa, Nellore, and Ongole enabled the Telugu Desam Party to dominate the municipal councils while opposition parties secured far fewer seats.

summary.headline: Telugu Desam Party-led alliance wins 12 of 13 mayoral posts in Andhra Pradesh
summary.summary: The Telugu Desam Party-led National Democratic Alliance secured twelve out of thirteen mayoral positions and nearly two-thirds of wards in urban local body elections across Andhra Pradesh on November 4, 2026. The results dealt a blow to the YSR Congress Party, which won only the Anantapur mayoral post. Polling covered thirteen municipal corporations and eighty-seven municipalities amid disruptions from two cyclones.

summary.headline: Supreme Court says India fertility drop makes two-child penalties outdated
summary.summary: The Supreme Court of India ruled on November 4, 2026, that laws penalising individuals for having more than two children have lost relevance due to falling fertility rates. A Bench led by Justice P.S. Narasimha stated that the 2003 Javed judgment requires reconsideration as demographic shifts point toward an ageing population. The court protected an elected official from disqualification under the Maharashtra law.

card.description: ‘The foundation of such laws, that is, the fear of overpopulation, has crumbled due to demographic changes in the past few decades’, says Bench

summary.headline: South Africa holds municipal elections amid declining support for governing party
summary.summary: South Africa held municipal elections on November 4, 2026, as growing public anger over corruption and failing services threatened the African National Congress. The ruling party fell below 50% support in 2021 and could drop further, potentially leading to unstable coalitions. President Cyril Ramaphosa acknowledged governance failures while expressing optimism. Polling stations closed at 9 p.m., with results expected by Sunday.

Tehran maintains control over the vital energy conduit and demands concessions from Washington before reopening the passage.

summary.headline: Bangladesh wage board agrees to revise garment worker pay structure from December
summary.summary: Bangladesh's newly formed wage board agreed on November 4, 2026, to implement a revised pay scale for garment workers starting in December following five days of protests and labour unrest. Workers have demanded an increase in the monthly minimum wage from 12,500 taka to 30,000 taka. Clashes occurred in Savar and Gazipur as protests disrupted spring and summer export order production.

summary.summary: Abdul El-Sayed, a physician and epidemiologist, defeated Republican former Representative Mike Rogers with 52.5% of the vote to become the first Muslim member of the United States Senate. summary.headline: India's 2027 census criteria for urban settlements
summary.summary: Published on November 4, 2026, details emerged regarding India's upcoming 2027 Census classifications. Settlements will be designated as urban if notified as statutory towns or if they meet specific criteria, including a minimum population of 5,000, a density of 400 persons per square kilometre, and at least 75 percent male workers in non-agricultural employment.

summary.headline: U.S. midterm elections feature historic firsts for governors and senators
summary.summary: Voters across the United States elected several groundbreaking candidates during the November 3, 2026, midterm elections. summary.headline: Survey reveals specific migration corridors from northeastern states to southern India
summary.summary: A survey conducted by Seven Sisters Development Assistance across 14 administrative blocks in Assam, Meghalaya, and Tripura revealed distinct migration corridors for employment in southern India. Published on November 5, 2026, the study covered 693 households, noting that 88 percent of individuals migrated due to local job shortages. Karnataka emerged as the top destination, attracting 22.7 percent of the outflow. Researchers found that median monthly earnings stood at 15,000 rupees, with personal networks rather than formal institutions driving the relocations.

card.summary: Hundreds of thousands of workers marched across France on November 5, 2026, to protest the rising cost of living and demand wage increases. The CGT union reported participation in 73 cities, while the Education Ministry noted 16 percent of teachers joined the strike. Authorities deployed 70,000 security personnel to manage the largely peaceful demonstrations.
card.description: The demonstrations come as the eurozone's second largest economy battles to redress its finances, six months ahead of elections to replace centrist President Emmanuel Macron

summary.headline: Sheikh Hasina confirms plan to return to Bangladesh from exile
summary.summary: Former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina stated she will return to Bangladesh from India in December despite facing a death sentence for crimes against humanity. Ousted in 2024, Hasina rejected the tribunal's verdict and alleged systemic suppression of her Awami League party. The current government, led by Tarique Rahman, has not commented on her potential arrival.

The current government, led by Tarique Rahman, has not commented on her potential arrival.
card.description: Hasina's planned return comes as her party faces an uncertain future amid a sweeping crackdown. The party remains banned, with senior leaders arrested or driven into exile.

summary.headline: Gadi Eisenkot emerges as favourite to form new Israeli government
summary.summary: Gadi Eisenkot emerged as the favourite to form an Israeli government on Thursday after President Isaac Herzog held consultations following the October 27 election. Neither Eisenkot nor Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu secured a parliamentary majority. United Torah Judaism declined to recommend Netanyahu, while Arab-Israeli lawmaker Mansour Abbas recommended Eisenkot, who insists on closing military service exemptions for religious students.

summary.headline: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu faces weakened position after coalition partner withholds support

card.headline: BJP faces political risks from partisan electoral map redrawing
card.title: What the BJP should learn from Trump’s redistricting failure
card.summary: The Bharatiya Janata Party should consider the Republican Party's recent failures in the United States when pursuing electoral boundary changes. Despite Republican efforts to flip seats through gerrymandering, the party suffered significant losses. Recent by-election results in Bihar suggest that constituency mapping cannot guarantee success if a party loses support from its traditional voter base.
card.description: Gerrymandering assumes that voting preferences remain unchanged between election cycles; but when the traditional supporters of a party turn against it, constituency maps matter little.

summary.headline: India achieves 1.7% compressed biogas blending in first half of fiscal
summary.summary: India reached a 1.7% blending rate for compressed biogas with natural gas between April and September, according to the Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board. The regulator highlighted that expanding pipeline connectivity to plants is essential to improve capacity utilisation and ensure consistent gas offtake.

Launched in 1977, the spacecraft carries a golden record containing human sounds and images intended for potential interstellar discovery. The mission, which passed Neptune in 1990, continues to provide a humbling perspective on our planet's place.

summary.headline: Amazon rainforest now releases more carbon dioxide than it absorbs
summary.summary: A study conducted between 2010 and 2024 reveals that the Amazon rainforest has transitioned from a carbon sink into a net carbon source. Researchers using airplanes to measure atmospheric CO2 levels found that deforestation and forest fires have decimated the region's capacity to offset human-induced emissions, rendering the forest unable to mitigate regional anthropogenic pollution levels.

summary.headline: India mandates visas for undocumented minority migrants
summary.summary: The Indian Ministry of Home Affairs has amended the Immigration and Foreigners Order to require undocumented non-Muslim migrants from Afghanistan, Bangladesh, and Pakistan who entered India before December 31, 2024, to obtain visas for continued stay. The notification also updates travel document requirements for Indian, Nepali, and Bhutanese citizens crossing borders and clarifies various refugee exemption categories.

summary.headline: Cosmoserve Space unveils India first private space debris facility
summary.summary: Hyderabad-based startup Cosmoserve Space unveiled Base 1 on November 6, 2026, marking India’s first private space debris recovery and satellite servicing facility. Inaugurated by Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh and Telangana Minister D. Sridhar Babu, the facility features advanced laboratories for space robotics and orbital capture. Founder Dr. Chiranjeevi Phanindra stated that the company plans to conduct a full-scale debris capture demonstration by 2027 using its proprietary dual spacecraft architecture.

summary.headline: Four killed and two missing after SUV plunges into river in Uttarakhand

Authorities are currently investigating the accident.

summary.headline: NPCI defends new merchant discount rate charge in Supreme Court
summary.summary: The National Payments Corporation of India defended its newly introduced merchant discount rate in the Supreme Court on November 5, 2026. Represented by Additional Solicitor General N. Venkataraman, the corporation stated that zero-MDR was unsustainable for the expanding Unified Payments Interface ecosystem. The amended framework imposes a 0.4 percent charge on person-to-merchant transactions exceeding two thousand rupees while keeping ninety-six percent of merchant payments and all peer-to-peer transactions entirely free.

Authorities confirmed that no explosives were found during security searches, and investigations into the source of the emails are ongoing.

summary.headline: United States markets slide as technology sector leads heavy losses
summary.summary: United States markets declined sharply on Thursday following sweeping Democratic midterm election victories. summary.headline: Nigerian court invalidates opposition presidential candidate Atiku Abubakar's nomination

summary.headline: Australian department store David Jones enters voluntary administration after 188 years

The suspended students had faced disciplinary action for allegedly staging a mock cremation of Vice-Chancellor Ciza Thomas and damaging her vehicle. The court cited a 2017 precedent stating that political activities like hunger strikes have no place in academic institutions. The aggrieved students subsequently appealed to the Supreme Court.
card.description: Division Bench of Justices Anil K. Narendran and S. Muralee Krishna said educational Institutions are meant for imparting education and not campus politics; by their political ambition, the political parties cannot hold to ransom the educational institution or the right of the civilised students to receive education, the Bench stated

The updated policy ensures voters can retain their historical identification numbers.

summary.headline: Nithya Raman elected as mayor of Los Angeles
summary.summary: Nithya Raman won the mayoral election in Los Angeles, becoming the first Asian-American to lead the city and the latest democratic socialist to secure a major United States municipality. Born in India and raised in the United States, Raman focused her campaign on expanding affordable housing, combating homelessness, and protecting immigrant communities. According to the Los Angeles Homeless Services Authority, the city housed roughly forty-four thousand homeless residents as of 2025. Raman previously defeated incumbent David Ryu in 2019 to join the city council.

Led by Director Vinay Kumar Nandicoori, the team used CRISPR technology to demonstrate that disrupting SecA1 and Tat pathways impairs bacterial survival. Published in Molecular and Cellular Proteomics, the discovery offers potential new treatment targets for tuberculosis.

card.summary: A Kuala Lumpur high court ruled that former Prime Minister Najib Razak will serve the remainder of his reduced six-year sentence under house arrest following a conditional pardon. Judge Aslam Zainuddin delivered the decision on Tuesday after an earlier delay by the attorney general over legal interpretations. Najib remains convicted in connection with the 1Malaysia Development Berhad scandal and faces additional prison terms.
card.description: Najib, 73, was jailed for his role in looting the now-defunct sovereign wealth fund 1MDB.

summary.headline: France summons Iranian ambassador following supermarket refrigerator cyberattack
summary.summary: France summoned Iran ambassador to Paris to lodge a protest after accusing Tehran of orchestrating a cyberattack that targeted supermarket refrigerators on October 11 and 12. Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot stated the incident ruined millions of euros in perishable food across multiple store chains. Paris prosecutors initiated an investigation into an Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps cyber unit regarding the sabotage.

A company spokesperson told Reuters that reliance on high-skilled visa programmes had decreased alongside shifting client needs. The announcement follows increased pressure from the administration of President Donald Trump regarding the employment of foreign technology workers.
card.description: Announcement follows Trump administration crackdown on visa programmes for skilled foreign workers.

card.summary: Kenya has discharged its seventh and final Ebola patient, marking a key milestone in its response to an outbreak that began in October following an importation from the Democratic Republic of Congo. Health Minister Aden Duale announced that all tracked contacts have completed monitoring, leaving the nation to begin a 42-day countdown toward an official virus-free declaration under World Health Organization guidelines.
card.description: The country begins a 42-day countdown to being declared Ebola-free, provided no new cases are recorded.

summary.headline: Cairo court adjourns retrial of journalist Lina Attalah amid UN criticism
summary.summary: A criminal court in Cairo adjourned the retrial of Mada Masr editor-in-chief Lina Attalah until 18 November after defence lawyers requested a new judge. The legal proceedings follow a recent conviction for operating a website without a licence and a separate in absentia sentence. The United Nations has criticized the case, warning of widening assaults on press freedom by Egyptian authorities against independent newsrooms.

Sent on November 6, the appeal addresses reported restrictions on access to water, education, healthcare, and identity documents, alongside unverified claims of an impending expulsion order set by local authorities.

card.description: The size of the demonstrations has been seen as an indicator of public discontent before a snap election set for this month, in which the right-wing opposition is expected to defeat Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez

summary.headline: Atmospheric conditions cause firecracker emissions to linger
summary.summary: Emissions from firecrackers can remain trapped in the air when weak local winds prevent pollutants from dispersing effectively. According to published reports on November 12, 2026, continuous firecracker use over several hours causes fine particles to accumulate near the source faster than cleaner air can dilute them. Local weather patterns and atmospheric stability directly influence how long these harmful smoke particles persist in the environment.

card.summary: Alice Huang, an executive accused of spying for Beijing while linked to Nvidia founder Jensen Huang, entered Taiwan eight times between 2024 and 2025 using a Hong Kong passport, according to Mainland Affairs Council Minister Chiu Chui-cheng on Thursday, November 12, 2026. Taiwanese officials stated she entered under standard business visitor status and security agencies are currently investigating the matter.
card.description: Taiwan, a dominant player in the global semiconductor industry, sits at the centre of strategic competition between the United States and China, which claims the self-ruled island as part of its territory

summary.headline: Ugandan police investigate deaths of four pupils in suspected poisoning
summary.summary: Ugandan police are investigating the deaths of four girls aged nine to 11 at Ta'aliim Primary School and Quran Memorisation Centre in Kampala on Tuesday, November 11, 2026, suspected to result from poisoning after eating oranges shared by a fellow pupil. The head teacher has been arrested to assist investigations, while post-mortem examinations are conducted to determine the exact cause of death.

summary.headline: BBC Verify finds discrepancies in Delhi air pollution data during Diwali
summary.summary: BBC Verify revealed that official datasets from the Central Pollution Control Board omitted hourly particulate matter readings exceeding 1,000 micrograms during Diwali celebrations in Delhi. Researchers warned that excluding extreme pollution episodes from monitoring stations misrepresents actual air quality levels and prevents accurate daily averages, potentially undermining public trust in official figures across the capital city.

summary.headline: Putin pushes for European security overhaul during peace talks with US envoys

Meanwhile, Ukrainian drone attacks continue to target Russian infrastructure despite ongoing diplomatic efforts to broker a peace agreement.

card.title: All departing U.S. flights grounded due to communication outage
card.summary: All departing flights across the United States were grounded on Friday, November 13, 2026, following a temporary telecommunications outage affecting air route traffic control centres. The Federal Aviation Administration ordered the rare national stop out of an abundance of caution, stranding tens of thousands of passengers and causing widespread travel disruption. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin confirmed there was no indication of a nefarious attack.
card.description: The incident marked only the second time such an alert was given in U.S. airspace since the 9/11 attacks; Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said there was no sign of a threat to the country and “this isn’t another 9/11”

summary.headline: Cruise ship passengers rescued following collision in New Orleans
summary.summary: Approximately 130 people aboard the American Heritage cruise ship were rescued after a collision with the cargo vessel Atlantic Asphalt on the Mississippi River in New Orleans on Friday. Thirty-two individuals sustained non-critical injuries and were hospitalised, while no people remained unaccounted for. Officials including Mayor Helena Moreno hailed the successful rescue operation as a miracle on the Mississippi.

summary.headline: Ugandan army arrests senior generals amid presidential succession political tensions
summary.summary: The Ugandan military detained at least a dozen senior officers during a crackdown led by army commander General Muhoozi Kainerugaba. The arrests, which include former intelligence chiefs, coincide with political divisions over the presidential succession of long-ruling President Yoweri Museveni. While officials defended the actions as anti-corruption measures, analysts argue the moves target officers opposing the general's ambitions.

summary.headline: London police open sex offence investigation into comedian David Walliams
summary.summary: The Metropolitan Police in London launched an investigation into non-recent serious sexual offences involving British comedian and author David Walliams following media reports accusing him of grooming and abuse. Walliams, who is 55 years old and denies all allegations, has been dropped by his literary agency and had several shows removed by the BBC. The probe follows investigative reports published by ITV News and The Guardian.

summary.headline: Afghanistan completes a road to the Chinese border despite closure
summary.summary: Afghanistan completed an unpaved road through the Wakhan Corridor to the Chinese border in Badakhshan province. Funded by the Afghan government at a cost of 365 million afghanis, the project aims to boost trade. However, Beijing has not opened the border or commented on the route, as China prioritizes strict regional security guarantees over commercial access due to ongoing threat concerns.

summary.headline: Clint Eastwood directed the sports film Invictus about Nelson Mandela
summary.summary: The cinematic film Invictus portrays how South African President Nelson Mandela utilized the 1995 Rugby World Cup to unite the nation following the end of apartheid. Directed by Clint Eastwood, the movie stars Morgan Freeman as Mandela and Matt Damon as Springboks captain Francois Pienaar, highlighting how sport served as a crucial tool for national reconciliation during a pivotal historical period.

summary.headline: Amazon plans World Product Graph to index global online shopping data
summary.summary: Amazon is reportedly planning to build the World Product Graph, a comprehensive data vault containing information on products sold anywhere across the internet. According to Reuters, the initiative aims to reduce user reliance on platforms like Reddit and Google while improving the accuracy of Amazon’s shopping assistant, Alexa for Shopping. Amazon stated that the internal document does not necessarily reflect current plans.
